items.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries. These documents supplement information from the LLM's pre-existing training data. This allows LLMs to use domain-specific and/or updated information that is not available in the training data. For example, this enables LLM-based chatbots to access internal company data or generate responses based on authoritative sources. The technique was first proposed in 2020 and has since become a widely adopted approach in modern AI systems.

Urbyte said an agent credential tried to cross into another tenant's resource boundary and obtain administrative permission beyond its assigned scope. Both requests were denied before the provider was invoked, while an authorised research action proceeded and generated a receipt that was reused when the same action was delivered again. items.title: When AI goes rogue, who should keep it in check? - Harvard Law School | Harvard Law School
items.summary:
One of the key reasons for Hadfield and Ramakrishnan’s growing anxiety: a July 2026 cyberattack by rogue AI agents on Hugging Face, a platform that hosts open-source AI models and datasets. [...] “The thing that I think actually disturbs me the most about the Hugging Face incident is that there’s a lot of evidence that at least at various points, the agents know what they’re doing is wrong. They say, ‘Oh, this is against our instructions, or would contravene ethical norms, but there is no other way to do what we’re trying to do,’” he said. [...] This behavior is sometimes called “reward hacking,” Ramakrishnan said. With the Hugging Face attack, he added, “This is the first big incident where I think you have, I wouldn’t say unambiguous, but really quite strong evidence of this phenomenon.”

While Ramakrishnan was careful to say that he believed that “some of the upsides [of AI] could be very large” — discovering a cure for cancer, for example — he also saw a looming question about human purpose.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: After testing FAN SZN by @IPXExchange here’s exactly what drives Aura:
items.summary:
After testing FAN SZN by @IPXExchange here’s exactly what drives Aura:

1. Daily streak is the biggest multiplier  
Starts at 2.0x and climbs toward 2.9x. It multiplies every content score, so protecting the streak matters more than posting heavily on a single day.

2. Alfred AI rewards useful content  
Clear, practical breakdowns of how the system works score higher than pure promo. Structured explanations consistently land in the upper range.

3. Plus-Ones only count with real activity  
Aura is given when invited people complete the Fan Check and build a streak — not just when they join.

4. Follower count has limited impact  
It mainly affects starting Social Aura. After that, contribution drives ranking more than audience size.

I’m in Afrobeats Nation and currently focusing on streak consistency + clear explanations. This approach has produced the best scores so far.

The interesting part isn’t just how real she looks. It’s how memorable she is.

Here’s why the character works:

1. The silver hair is the signature.
You recognize her instantly. That’s a huge advantage in a feed full of interchangeable AI faces.

2. Her style creates the contrast.
She’s older and effortlessly stylish. Clothes and sunglasses feel like natural extensions of her personality.

3. She says exactly what she thinks.
That blunt, confident attitude gives you a reason to keep watching. Main-character energy doesn’t have an age limit.

The takeaway: give your AI character a recognizable look and a point of view.

A lot of creators choose a face and skip the personality.

items.title: Transformer (deep learning)
items.summary: In deep learning, the transformer is a family of artificial neural network architectures based on the multi-head attention mechanism, in which input data such as text, images, or audio is converted to a sequence of numerical representations called tokens, and each token is converted into a vector through an embedding layer. At each layer, each token is then contextualized within the scope of the context window with other (unmasked) tokens via a parallel multi-head attention mechanism, allowing the signal for key tokens to be amplified and less important tokens to be diminished. Because self-attention alone is permutation-invariant, transformers inject positional information, typically through positional encodings or learned positional embeddings, so token order can affect the output.
